subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Relativity of Rich
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Relativity of Rich.

hook.text: Earning $200,000 in Manhattan feels middle-class. The same income in rural Mississippi feels wealthy.

buildup.text: We judge wealth relative to peers, neighbors, and local costs. Absolute income matters less than relative position.

discovery.text: Luttmer found that neighbors' income negatively predicts happiness. A raise at work feels hollow if colleagues got.

twist.text: This means moving to a richer area can make you feel poorer even if your income stays the same.

climax.text: Financial satisfaction improves when you stop comparing sideways and start comparing backward: where you were a year.

punchline.text: Rich is a feeling, not a number. Choose your reference.

quiz.question: Why can high earners still feel 'poor'?
options: They compare to even higher-earning peers in their environment
High earners have more expenses by law
